body_markdown:
When summer gear is still sitting outside after the first cold snap, spring can arrive with dirty cushions, rusty bike chains, and a grill that needs far more attention than anyone wants to give it.


A simple[winter storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/public-storage/what-should-you-take-out-of-storage-before-winter.html) routine can help. Clean off dirt and debris, let everything dry fully, follow manufacturer guidance for equipment, and decide what can stay at home versus what can move to an appropriate seasonal storage spot.


## Key Takeaways


- Clean and dry summer gear before cold, wet weather settles in.
- Patio furniture, cushions, bicycles, and folding outdoor items benefit from a dry winter storage spot.
- Grills and lawn mowers require manufacturer-guided care and an appropriate at-home storage location.
- Covers can help keep leaves, dust, and debris off outdoor furniture.
- A short spring checklist can make the first warm weekend much easier.


## Winter Storage Checklist


Before furniture covers come out and summer gear disappears for the season, give everything a quick once-over. You’re looking for the small things that can create bigger headaches later: leftover dirt, trapped moisture, loose parts, and repairs that are much easier to remember now than next spring.


Use this checklist before putting items away:


- Brush off dirt, leaves, pollen, grass clippings, and other debris.
- Let cushions, furniture, bicycles, and accessories dry completely.
- Check for loose hardware, worn covers, or items that may need attention in spring.
- Follow the manufacturer’s instructions for grills and lawn equipment.
- Write down any repairs, replacement parts, or tune-ups to revisit later.


A few minutes now can make outdoor season feel like a return to fun, not a weekend-long cleanup project.


## Clean Patio Furniture Before Covering It


Patio chairs and tables collect more than you notice during summer. Dirt settles into chair frames, leaves get wedged between slats, and pollen has a way of appearing in places that seem impossible.


Wipe down hard surfaces with a material-appropriate cloth, then let the furniture dry fully before covering it.[Outdoor cushions](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/storage-tips/how-to-store-patio-cushions.html) should also be cleaned according to their care tags and completely dry before going into a closet, bin, or other enclosed space.


For easier storage, fold tables, stack compatible chairs, and gather smaller pieces such as lanterns, tabletop decor, and outdoor games together.


**Patio Item** **Winter Storage Tip**


Chairs Stack or fold compatible pieces after cleaning


Tables Fold when possible or cover in a dry area


Cushions Clean, dry fully, and place in a dry indoor spot


Umbrellas Close, clean, dry, and store according to manufacturer guidance


Small decor Gather into one labeled bin for spring


Use breathable furniture covers when possible. Covers that trap moisture can create a less-than-welcome surprise when patio season returns.


## Give Your Grill a Proper Winter Break


A grill is much nicer to return to in spring when it gets a quick clean before winter. Remove food debris and ash, wipe down exterior surfaces, and check the manufacturer’s seasonal-care instructions for your specific model.


A fitted cover can help keep leaves, dust, and winter debris off an outdoor grill. Keep the grill in an appropriate at-home area and follow local requirements and manufacturer guidance for seasonal care.


For grills with removable accessories, consult the manufacturer’s instructions before deciding where to[store those pieces](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/storage-tips/how-to-store-grills-and-outdoor-cooking-equipment.html) during the winter months.


## Clear Grass and Dirt From Lawn Equipment


[Lawn equipment](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/storage-tips/lawn-equipment-storage-tips.html) has usually earned a break by the end of summer. Start by brushing away grass clippings and dirt from the outside of the mower and other yard tools.


Then follow the manufacturer’s winter-maintenance instructions for your specific model. A dry garage, shed, or another appropriate at-home area can help keep equipment out of winter weather.


Smaller yard tools can also use a reset before spring. Remove dirt, dry them, and group them together so they are easier to find when warmer weather returns.


## Store Bicycles Away From Winter Weather


Bicycles can handle everyday use, but long stretches of rain, snow, and moisture can be tough on exposed parts.


Wipe off mud and moisture, then let the bike dry before putting it away. A garage, indoor area, wall hook, or covered space can keep it off the ground and out of the weather. If you’re[storing your bike](https://www.publicstorage.com/blog/storage-tips/how-to-store-a-bike.html) in a covered outdoor area, choose a cover that fits without holding moisture against the frame.


When spring comes around, check the tires, brakes, chain, and any parts that may need attention before the first ride.


## Find Room for Seasonal Items


Not every home has a garage, shed, basement, or spare closet for patio furniture, bicycles, and outdoor cushions. When summer gear starts competing with everyday items, it can make a home feel crowded quickly.


Clean, dry patio furniture, folding tables, cushions, and bicycles may be eligible for[seasonal self-storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/storage-solutions/seasonal-storage) when they meet facility rules. Check current availability, access details, and item restrictions before reserving.


**If You’re Putting Away…** **Consider…**


Cushions and small patio items A dry closet, storage bench, or labeled bin


Folding chairs and compact tables A garage wall, shed, or eligible storage space


Bicycles A wall hook, indoor corner, or eligible storage space


Larger patio furniture A covered area or eligible self-storage space


Small outdoor accessories One labeled bin near other seasonal items


Grills and lawn mowers belong in appropriate at-home locations and should follow manufacturer guidance rather than going into a storage unit.


## Make a Quick Spring List


Before closing the garage door or putting away the last cushion, make a short note for spring.


Maybe a chair needs a new foot cap. Maybe the bike could use a tune-up. Maybe a cushion has reached the end of its outdoor life. A note in your phone can save you from trying to remember everything when the first warm weekend arrives.


## FAQs About Storing Summer Gear for Winter


**How do I store patio furniture for winter?**


Clean off dirt and debris, let furniture dry completely, and use breathable covers or a dry indoor area when possible. Stack or fold compatible pieces to save space.


**Should I cover my grill in winter?**


A fitted cover can help keep leaves and winter debris off an outdoor grill. Follow the manufacturer’s seasonal-care instructions and keep the grill in an appropriate at-home location.


**How do I store a lawn mower for winter?**


Brush away grass clippings and dirt, then follow the manufacturer’s winter-maintenance instructions for your model. Keep the mower in a dry garage, shed, or another appropriate at-home area.


**Where should I store my bicycle in winter?**


A garage, indoor area, wall hook, covered space, or eligible storage space can work well. Clean and dry the bike first, then keep it away from extended exposure to wet weather.


**Can I use self-storage for patio furniture?**


Clean, dry patio furniture and other eligible seasonal items may be suitable for self-storage. Check current facility rules, availability, and item restrictions before reserving.


## Make Spring Easier for Future You


Summer gear doesn’t need a huge winter project. A little cleaning, drying, and planning can help everything stay ready for warmer days ahead.


When larger patio items or bicycles are taking up everyday space at home, explore[Public Storage](https://www.publicstorage.com/find-storage) for current unit availability and seasonal storage options near you.
